data.name: Montenegro
data.summary: Montenegro (euro, non-EU) taxes residents' worldwide capital gains at a flat 15% (no municipal surtax on gains) and dividends at 15% plus a municipal surtax of up to 15% of the tax (17.25% in Podgorica). No wealth tax, and no inheritance or gift tax for children (only real estate transfer tax for other heirs). No special tax regime for wealthy arrivals.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.eligibility: Tax resident if domiciled, centre of vital interests in Montenegro, or 183+ days in the tax year. Non-citizens need a residence permit.

capital_gains.summary: Resident individuals pay a flat 15% personal income tax on capital gains from shares, securities and real estate, worldwide. Gain = sale price minus acquisition price. No holding-period exemption for securities. The municipal surtax (prirez) is not charged on capital-gains tax: the Law on Financing Local Self-Government (Art. 8(3)) levies it only on the tax on personal earnings, self-employment income, income from property and property rights, and capital income (dividends, interest).
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Exempt: sale of the taxpayer's only and main residence; transfers between spouses linked to marriage, divorce or inheritance; gifts to first-order relatives (spouse, children). Capital losses can be set against gains of the same year.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Tax residents (domicile, centre of vital interests, or 183+ days) are taxed on worldwide gains.
capital_gains.regional_differences: PIT is national. The municipal surtax does not apply to capital gains (Law on Financing Local Self-Government, Sl. list CG 3/2019, Art. 8(3) lists the taxes it is levied on, and capital gains are not among them).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Since Sl. list CG 152/22 (in force 30 Dec 2022) capital, capital-gains and property income is taxed at 15% (previously 9%). The tax authority can substitute market value when shares in a company are sold below market value.

open_questions: Current consolidated text of the PIT law after Sl. list CG 152/22 and later amendments could not be opened; the 15% rate relies on PwC (reviewed Aug 2026) and Unija/ePorezi summaries.
No exit tax for individuals was found, but this was not confirmed against legislation.
The surtax conclusion rests on the 2019 text of the local-finance law (Paragraf, last updated 2021); later amendments were not checked.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Flat 15% PIT rate on net capital gains (law amended by Sl. list CG 152/22). No municipal surtax: Art. 8(3) of the local-finance law does not list tax on capital gains in the surtax base.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Frequent trading could be treated as self-employment (entrepreneurial) income, taxed at progressive 0/9/15% plus social contributions; no specific guidance found.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: No holding-period exemption for shares or real estate (other than the main-residence exemption).
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide taxation for residents with a foreign tax credit capped at Montenegrin tax; treaties prevail.

dividends.summary: Dividends received by resident individuals are capital income taxed at a flat 15% on the gross amount, withheld by a Montenegrin payer; foreign dividends are self-assessed at 15% with a credit for foreign tax up to the Montenegrin tax. The municipal surtax applies on top, because Art. 8(3) of the Law on Financing Local Self-Government includes the tax on capital income in its base: up to 15% of the tax in Podgorica and Cetinje (15% x 1.15 = 17.25%), up to 13% elsewhere (16.95%).
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: Interest on bonds of the State, the Central Bank or local governments is not taxable capital income (from 19 Nov 2025, Sl. list CG 133/25).
dividends.regional_differences: Municipal surtax on the tax on capital income, set by each municipality: up to 15% in Podgorica (Glavni grad) and Cetinje (Prijestonica), up to 13% elsewhere (Art. 8(1)–(2)). Effective 17.25% in Podgorica; the Tivat and Budva rates were not checked (at most 16.95%).
dividends.important_exceptions: Pre-2023 rate was 9%; some secondary sources still quote 9%.

dividends.withholding_outbound: 15% WHT on dividends paid to residents and non-residents (30% to entities in listed tax havens), reducible by treaty.
dividends.treaty_network: 47 treaties per PwC, including most EU states, UK, Switzerland, UAE, China; no treaty with the United States.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Corporate shareholders: dividends from resident companies are generally excluded from the CIT base; not researched in depth.

wealth_tax.summary: Montenegro has no net wealth tax and no recurring levy on financial assets.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Annual real estate tax at municipal rates of 0.25%-1% of market value (PwC). A 2025 amendment to the real estate tax law was enacted; its detail was not reviewed.

inheritance.summary: There is no inheritance or gift tax on money, securities or other movables. Inherited or gifted real estate is subject to real estate transfer tax (3%/5%/6% progressive), but first-order heirs (children, spouse) and the deceased's parents, and first-order donees and the donor's spouse, are exempt.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Art. 14(1)(1) Law on Real Estate Transfer Tax: no tax for the first-order heir, spouse and parent of the deceased, or a first-order donee and the donor's spouse.
inheritance.eligibility_conditions: Exemption depends on the family relationship only.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Other heirs pay real estate transfer tax: 3% up to EUR 150,000, 5% EUR 150,000-500,000, 6% above (since 1 Jan 2024). Gifts to first-order relatives are also exempt from capital gains tax.

income.name: Montenegro

income_tax.summary: Salaries are taxed at 0% up to EUR 700 a month, 9% from EUR 700 to 1,000 and 15% above (EUR 8,400 and 12,000 a year); entrepreneurial income uses the same annual thresholds (EUR 8,400 and 12,000) from 1 January 2026. A municipal surtax of 15% of the tax applies in Podgorica (13% in most other towns), giving effective marginal rates of 10.35% and 17.25%. Employees pay 10% pension contributions (capped, EUR 75,453 in 2025) and 0.5% unemployment insurance.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: UNVERIFIED: the self-employed rate is assumed equal to the employee rate (10.5%: 10% pension + 0.5% unemployment, health abolished January 2022 per eporezi.me). Neither PwC nor eporezi.me states regular entrepreneur rates or base; eporezi.me gives only the new (1 January 2026) supplementary entrepreneurial activity category for people employed elsewhere, with a base of 60% / 100% / 150% of the average monthly wage by turnover (up to EUR 9,000 / EUR 15,000 / above), rates not stated. Entrepreneurs can opt for lump-sum taxation if the previous year's turnover is at most EUR 30,000. Employee social_security_deductible: Based on professional and secondary guides, not Poreska uprava or the statute; medium-low confidence.
income_tax.local_tax_note: Podgorica surtax: 15% of the income tax (13% in most municipalities, 10% in Budva). The brackets already include it (9% x 1.15 = 10.35%, 15% x 1.15 = 17.25%). The 0% band stands in for the EUR 700 monthly allowance.

regimes.name: Digital nomad temporary residence
regimes.description: Temporary residence for non-EU remote workers earning at least three times the Montenegrin minimum wage (roughly EUR 1,800 to 2,400 a month per Remote Work Europe) from non-Montenegrin employers or clients, valid up to two years and renewable for the same period; the status was codified in the Law on Foreigners in January 2026 (eporezi.me). Tax: the Personal Income Tax Law exempts a person's income from personal earnings OR self-employment 'from an employer not registered in Montenegro on the basis of acquired digital nomad status under the law governing the residence and work of foreigners' (wording quoted by the Unija law-firm page on the Sl. list CG 152/22 amendments; Remote Work Europe cites art. 32d). Because it exempts the holder's pay by employer registration and status, not by where the work is done, it covers work performed in Montenegro (covers_local_work true). Social contributions reportedly do not apply (eporezi.me, Remote Work Europe). A stay over 183 days can create tax residency; how the status interacts with that test is not stated.
regimes.duration_note: Up to two years, renewable for the same period (realistic maximum four).

succession.name: Montenegro
succession.summary: Descendants and the spouse are guaranteed half of their intestate share, with a smaller share for other close relatives. Montenegro has no trust law and is outside the Hague Trusts Convention. Foundations are limited to non-profit use.
succession.reserved_share: Descendants, adoptees and spouse: 1/2 of the intestate share; parents and other heirs 1/3; Law on Succession (OG 74/2008). Article numbers not confirmed.
succession.foreign_law_note: The 2013 Law on Private International Law governs succession; whether a foreign national may choose their national law was not confirmed.
succession.trust_note: No trust law. Foundations are non-profit bodies under the Law on Non-Governmental Organisations.
open_questions: Statute article numbers and exact fractions for forced heirs outside descendants and spouse were not read in the primary text; confirm in the official gazette.
Whether a foreign national resident may choose a law for their estate under the current private international law act was not confirmed.

immigration.name: Montenegro
immigration.summary: Montenegro is not in the EU: EU citizens, like everyone else, need a temporary residence permit for stays beyond the visa-free period. Common routes are owning property (a minimum assessed value of EUR 150,000 for non-EU citizens from 2026; EU citizens are exempt from the value test), a remote-work permit, running a company, or employment. The citizenship-by-investment programme ended on 31 December 2022 and has not reopened.
immigration.naturalisation: Reported 10 years of continuous legal residence (5 years temporary, then 5 years permanent), with language and other tests; secondary sources.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Montenegro does not generally recognise dual nationality (IMI Daily); exceptions and treaty cases not checked.

routes.name: Temporary residence on property ownership
routes.summary: Owning real estate in Montenegro gives a renewable one-year residence permit, without the right to work. Since 17 January 2026 non-EU citizens need property assessed at EUR 150,000 or more.
routes.requirements: Amendments to the Law on Foreigners (in force 17 January 2026 per IMI Daily; adopted 31 December 2025): third-country nationals must own property with a tax-authority assessed value of at least EUR 150,000 (hold at least a half share; co-owners need EUR 150,000 per share-holder), prove actual use and pay property tax. Nationals of EU states, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland are excluded from the value test. The permit does not allow work or business. Permits issued before 17 January 2026 renew without the value test.
routes.investment_options: EUR 150,000 assessed value for non-EU citizens; no stated minimum for EU/EEA/Swiss citizens (property must still be owned).
routes.physical_presence: Actual use of the property; day count not sourced
routes.tax_note: A residence permit does not by itself make you tax resident; Montenegro uses a 183-day test and centre of interests.

routes.name: Temporary residence for digital nomads
routes.summary: Remote workers employed by or working for a foreign company can get a residence permit of up to two years, extendable once by up to two years.
routes.requirements: Work electronically for a foreign company or your own company not registered in Montenegro; enter legally; proof of financial means of support (no fixed amount published), accommodation, health insurance, a valid passport (3 months beyond the permit), clean record, and an employment contract or proof of remote work. Applied for in person at the Ministry of Internal Affairs office. Decision within 40 days.
routes.physical_presence: Reside in Montenegro for the permit period
routes.family: Spouse and children up to 18 can join.
routes.tax_note: Becoming tax resident after 183 days or centre of interests; permit alone does not decide tax residence.

routes.name: Residence as company owner or director (integrated work and residence)
routes.summary: Foreigners who register a Montenegrin company or business can obtain a combined work and residence permit. From 1 January 2027 owners of more than 51% must show the company paid at least EUR 5,000 a year in taxes and contributions to renew.
routes.requirements: Executive directors and registered entrepreneurs who own over 51% of a Montenegrin company: renewal conditional on EUR 5,000 paid in taxes and social contributions in the previous year (applies from 1 January 2027, per MD Realty; IMI Daily describes it as part of the 2026 amendments). EU, Iceland, Norway, Liechtenstein and Swiss nationals, permanent residents and holders of other grounds are exempt. Set-up capital and registration costs not researched.
